2. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES

2.1 The Ministry is responsible for the formulation, implementation, and oversight of public health policies and programmes within Cross River State, including the delivery of primary health care services to rural and underserved communities.

2.2 The Ministry has identified significant gaps in access to basic health services in rural communities across the State, particularly in the areas of maternal and child health, immunization coverage, malaria prevention, and health education.

2.3 In response to these gaps, the Ministry established the Rural Outreach Program 2024 (the "Program"), a statewide initiative designed to bring integrated primary health services closer to rural populations.

2.4 The Program aims to achieve the following objectives:

(a) Increase the proportion of pregnant women attending at least four (4) antenatal care visits in targeted communities;

(b) Increase the immunization coverage rate among children under one (1) year of age in targeted communities to at least 80%;

(c) Distribute long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) to households in malaria-endemic areas;

(d) Provide health education on hygiene, nutrition, and disease prevention to at least 100,000 individuals; and

(e) Strengthen community-based referral pathways to secondary health facilities.

2.5 The Contractor has demonstrated capacity and experience in delivering community-based health outreach services in Cross River State and has been selected to support the Ministry in achieving the Program objectives.

2.6 The Parties have agreed to enter into this Contract for the provision of the Services, on the terms and conditions set out below.

---

(a) perform the Services with due diligence, skill, and care, in accordance with the highest professional standards and best practices in community health outreach;

(b) comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and guidelines of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and Cross River State, including the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) protocols;

(c) ensure that all personnel engaged in the delivery of the Services are appropriately qualified, trained, and vetted;

(d) maintain a register of all personnel deployed under this Contract, including their qualifications and roles;

(e) cooperate fully with the Ministry, its Authorised Officer, and any designated monitors or auditors;

(f) provide the Ministry with all information and documentation reasonably required to verify performance of the Services;

(g) take all reasonable steps to ensure the safety and well-being of community members during outreach sessions;

(h) handle all health commodities and equipment with care, and in accordance with manufacturer instructions and Ministry guidelines;

(i) report immediately any serious incident, adverse event, or safety concern arising during the delivery of the Services;
(b) Termination for Default. (i) failure to achieve the performance targets set out in the Work Plan, without justifiable cause;

(ii) failure to maintain the insurance cover required under Clause 14;

(iii) engaging in fraudulent, corrupt, or collusive practices in connection with the performance of this Contract;

(iv) failure to comply with applicable laws and regulations, including the provisions of the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act, Cap C31, LFN 2004; or

(v) assignment, subcontracting, or delegation of any of its obligations under this Contract without the prior written consent of the Ministry.

(c) Termination for Insolvency. The Ministry may terminate this Contract with immediate effect by written notice to the Contractor if the Contractor becomes insolvent, is adjudicated bankrupt, commences winding-up proceedings, or makes any composition or arrangement with its creditors.

C.1.1 This Schedule sets out the operational protocols, service delivery standards, and reporting requirements for the Community Health Outreach component of the Agreement. **C.2 Definitions**

In this Schedule, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Outreach Session" means a single day of community-based service delivery at a designated site, comprising health education, screening, and referral activities.

"Mobile Team" means the personnel deployed by the Contractor for a given Outreach Session, including at minimum one (1) Community Health Extension Worker (CHEW), one (1) Nurse, and two (2) Community Health Volunteers (CHVs).

"Community Liaison Officer (CLO)" means the individual appointed by the Contractor and approved by the Ministry to facilitate community entry and mobilisation.

"Beneficiary Register" means the daily attendance log maintained in the format prescribed in Annex C-1.

**C.3 Service Delivery Standards**

C.3.1 Minimum Services. Each Outreach Session shall provide, at no cost to beneficiaries:

(a) Health education talks on topics approved by the Ministry's Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Unit, including but not limited to malaria prevention, maternal and child health, immunisation, and hygiene promotion;

(b) Blood pressure and blood glucose screening for adults;

(c) Weight and height measurement for children under five, with growth monitoring charts updated;

(d) Referral of suspected cases to the nearest primary health care facility, with a written referral slip issued to the beneficiary.

C.3.2 Session Duration and Timing. Each Outreach Session shall run for a minimum of six (6) hours, excluding set-up and break-down time. Sessions shall be scheduled between 08:00 and 16:00 WAT, unless a variation is approved in writing by the Ministry's M&E Unit at least five (5) working days in advance.

C.3.3 Team Composition. The Mobile Team shall be constituted as set out in Clause C.2 above. A record of team composition for each session shall be submitted with the session report.

C.3.4 Essential Supplies. The Contractor shall maintain a minimum stock level of consumables to cover two (2) consecutive Outreach Sessions, including but not limited to: blood pressure cuffs, glucometer strips, gloves, disinfectant, and health education materials. Stock levels shall be reported monthly to the M&E Unit.

**C.4 Planning and Mobilisation**

C.4.1 Monthly Work Plan. The Contractor shall submit a Monthly Outreach Work Plan to the M&E Unit no later than the 25th day of the preceding month. The Work Plan shall specify:

(a) the proposed dates and locations of each Outreach Session;

(b) the estimated number of beneficiaries per site;

(c) the name of the CLO responsible for each community;

(d) any logistical constraints anticipated.

C.4.2 Community Mobilisation. The CLO shall conduct community mobilisation at least seven (7) days before the scheduled session, using approved channels such as town criers, religious leaders, and women's group meetings. The mobilisation shall include information on the date, time, location, and services to be offered.

(a) the Contractor ceases to carry on its business or is otherwise unable to perform the Services;

(b) the Contractor is guilty of serious misconduct or fraud in the performance of the Services;

**SCHEDULE C — COMMUNITY HEALTH OUTREACH PROTOCOL**

**(Version 3.2, effective 15 January 2024)**

This Schedule C forms part of the Agreement between the Ministry of Health, Cross River State ("the Ministry") and the Contractor for the provision of Community Health Outreach Services. In the event of any conflict between this Schedule and the main body of the Agreement, the main body shall prevail, except where this Schedule expressly states otherwise.

**C.1 Purpose and Scope**

C.1.1 This Schedule sets out the operational protocols, service delivery standards, and reporting requirements for the Community Health Outreach component of the Agreement. It covers the planning, execution, and post-activity documentation of outreach sessions conducted in the rural and peri-urban communities listed in Schedule A (as amended from time to time).

C.1.2 The protocols herein are binding on the Contractor and any subcontractor engaged with the prior written consent of the Ministry under Clause 6.5 of the Agreement.

**C.2 Definitions**

In this Schedule, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Outreach Session" means a single day of community-based service delivery at a designated site, comprising health education, screening, and referral activities.

"Mobile Team" means the personnel deployed by the Contractor for a given Outreach Session, including at minimum one (1) Community Health Extension Worker (CHEW), one (1) Nurse, and two (2) Community Health Volunteers (CHVs).

"Community Liaison Officer (CLO)" means the individual appointed by the Contractor and approved by the Ministry to facilitate community entry and mobilisation.

"Beneficiary Register" means the daily attendance log maintained in the format prescribed in Annex C-1.

**C.3 Service Delivery Standards**

C.3.1 Minimum Services. Each Outreach Session shall provide, at no cost to beneficiaries:

(a) Health education talks on topics approved by the Ministry's Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Unit, including but not limited to malaria prevention, maternal and child health, immunisation, and hygiene promotion;

(b) Blood pressure and blood glucose screening for adults;

(c) Weight and height measurement for children under five, with growth monitoring charts updated;

(d) Referral of suspected cases to the nearest primary health care facility, with a written referral slip issued to the beneficiary.

C.3.2 Session Duration and Timing. Each Outreach Session shall run for a minimum of six (6) hours, excluding set-up and break-down time. Sessions shall be scheduled between 08:00 and 16:00 WAT, unless a variation is approved in writing by the Ministry's M&E Unit at least five (5) working days in advance.

C.3.3 Team Composition. The Mobile Team shall be constituted as set out in Clause C.2 above. The Contractor shall ensure that at least one (1) member of the Mobile Team is fluent in the predominant local language of the host community (e.g., Efik, Ejagham, or Bekwarra, as applicable). A record of team composition for each session shall be submitted with the session report.

C.3.4 Essential Supplies. The Contractor shall maintain a minimum stock level of consumables to cover two (2) consecutive Outreach Sessions, including but not limited to: blood pressure cuffs, glucometer strips, gloves, disinfectant, and health education materials. Stock levels shall be reported monthly to the M&E Unit.

**C.4 Planning and Mobilisation**

C.4.1 Monthly Work Plan. The Contractor shall submit a Monthly Outreach Work Plan to the M&E Unit no later than the 25th day of the preceding month. The Work Plan shall specify:

(a) the proposed dates and locations of each Outreach Session;

(b) the estimated number of beneficiaries per site;

(c) the name of the CLO responsible for each community;

(d) any logistical constraints anticipated.

C.4.2 Community Mobilisation. The CLO shall conduct community mobilisation at least seven (7) days before the scheduled session, using approved channels such as town criers, religious leaders, and women's group meetings. The mobilisation shall include information on the date, time, location, and services to be offered.
